metadata.title: Repeal the Durbin Amendment - Stop the Merchant Markup
metadata.author: Electronic Payments Coalition
metadata.shortDescription:
Debit and credit cards make it far more convenient to buy the things you need or love. Debit interchange convenience fees – the small charges retailers pay for the flexibility of accepting cards – make these transactions possible, secure, and reliable.

The Durbin amendment changed the way this once reasonable cost of business is calculated. Prices at big-box retailers should have been lowered for customers thanks to this change, it’s what retailers promised after all, but that hasn’t happened.

Big-box retailers have now pocketed $42 billion that was meant to go to you. This is what we call the Merchant Markup. Meanwhile, community banks, credit unions, and consumers are carrying the burden and being forced to eliminate debit card rewards and free checking accounts.

The Durbin amendment puts red tape and price controls on these purchases and must be immediately and completely repealed to restore the free market.

metadata.title: The Durbin Amendment: How Does it Affect My Business?
metadata.author: CenturyPaymentsInc
metadata.shortDescription:
If you're a merchant, you may be aware that the effects of the Durbin Amendment are in full swing. But as a business owner, do you really know what changes have occurred?

First here's a little recap.  The Durbin Amendment is an addendum to the Dodd-Frank Financial Reform and Consumer Protection Act that was passed by Congress in 2010. It essentially expanded the powers of the Federal Reserve allowing them to set interchange fees related to the processing of debit card transactions. The goal was to spur economic growth with lower fees allowing retailers to lower prices on their goods and increase consumer spending. As a merchant, this most notably affects your business when it comes to debit cards, specifically changes to the rules surrounding debit transactions. This is because, generally, interchange fees are charged by issuing banks for each payment accepted with a debit or credit card.

Prior to this amendment, banks were charging retailers an average of 44 cents per debit transaction. That doesn't sound like much, but according to the Federal Reserve, banks collected nearly $16 Billion on these fees annually. When the new amendment went into effect in October 2011, these fees were capped at only .21 cents per transaction. As a merchant, you're the winner as this capping of fees will allow you to reduce your amount of bank charges, and is an opportunity to lower prices and see increased consumer spending in your store. However, with such a loss in revenue for banks, they will most likely look for ways to make up that money in some way.

For more information on the Durbin Amendment, and for unique ways to leverage your payment processing while enjoying excellent customer service, visit our website.  Let us show you why we are in the top 15 of the fastest growing businesses on the Inc 500 List two years in a row!

metadata.title: A Truck Stop Just Killed the Fed's Debit-Card Fee Cap — But Your Checkout Won't Change Yet
metadata.author: LawLens
metadata.shortDescription:
A truck stop in North Dakota just killed the Federal Reserve's debit-card fee cap. But if you pay by debit tomorrow, nothing changes. Both things are true at the same time, and this video explains why.

We cover what the 21-cent cap actually is, how Corner Post's 2021 lawsuit survived the Supreme Court in 2024, what "incremental cost" really means (the marginal cost of one more swipe), why a single uniform number failed the statute, how the Loper Bright decision changed the rules for agencies, what the court deliberately did NOT do, and the second case in Kentucky that could split the circuits and send this to the Supreme Court.

Sources: Corner Post, Inc. v. Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, No. 25-3000 (8th Cir. Oct. 26, 2026); the Durbin Amendment; Regulation II; Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (2024); Linney's Pizza v. Board of Governors (E.D. Ky. 2025, on appeal in the Sixth Circuit).

This video is general information only, not legal advice.

metadata.author: Practical Ecommerce
metadata.shortDescription: The Durbin Amendment to the U.S. Dodd-Frank legislative package affects ecommerce merchants. That’s because the Amendment greatly lowers the rate — called interchange — that Visa and MasterCard charge for the processing of debit cards. But, importantly, it does not automatically lower the fees that merchants actually pay to their merchant account providers. Our guest today is a longtime veteran of the credit and debit card industry. He’s Sloane Bouchever, the founder of Interchange Plus Solutions, a merchant account provider, and he’s here to suggest ways for merchants to make certain they receive the lower debit card rates. He speaks with Practical Ecommerce’s Kerry Murdock.

metadata.title: How to Reduce Your B2B Credit Card Processing Fees with PayTrace Interchange Optimization and CEDP
metadata.author: PayTrace
metadata.shortDescription:
B2B payments are complex, but saving money on them doesn’t have to be. If your business accepts B2B and B2G credit cards, even if it’s only a fraction of your overall business, interchange optimization can help you reduce your credit card processing fees.

In this video, learn how interchange optimization helps B2B companies get better processing rates by qualifying transactions for Level 2 and Level 3 rates with Visa and Mastercard. 

 What we cover: 
- An overview of interchange and the value that optimized rates provide to merchants and cardholders
- How to leverage Level 3 processing to reduce the costs of card acceptance on B2B and B2G credit cards
- The recent changes to Level 3 processing introduced with Visa’s Commercial Enhanced Data Program (CEDP) and how merchants can comply with the requirements

Additional Resources:
- Interchange Optimization: https://paytrace.net/interchange-optimization
- PayTrace Product List for CEDP: https://paytrace.net/blog/paytrace-launches-product-list
- CEDP blog post: https://paytrace.net/blog/the-next-milestone-for-visas-cedp

Lower your interchange fees by 30%-40% regardless of your processors rate. Call today for your free quote 888 790 3450 https://www.revolution-payments.com/level-3-processing/

metadata.shortDescription:
If your customers pay with corporate or purchasing cards, missing transaction data could be pushing those sales into higher interchange categories.

Learn what Level 2 and Level 3 card data are, how to spot downgraded business card sales on your statement, and why enhanced data often fails to qualify. Then see a hypothetical walk-through of the free calculator.

Try the free tool (Level 2 & Level 3 Card Data Savings Calculator): https://touchsuite.com/tools/level-2-level-3-savings-calculator/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=level-2-level-3-savings-calculator
Book a 15-minute call with a payments specialist: https://go.oncehub.com/RobertSmith?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=level-2-level-3-savings-calculator

Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:11 What Level 2 and 3 mean
0:37 Check your statement
0:59 Why data fails to qualify
1:19 Worked example
1:50 Try it yourself

This video is general information, not financial or legal advice.
Estimates are based on published industry averages and are not a quote. Actual rates depend on card mix, ticket size, industry, and underwriting.

segments.text: If your customers pay with corporate or purchasing cards,
missing transaction data could be pushing
those sales into higher interchange categories.
Level 2 data usually adds the sales tax amount
and a customer code or purchase order number.
Level 3 adds line-item detail, like product code, quantity, unit price, and freight.
This extra detail can help business, corporate, purchasing,
and government card sales qualify for lower interchange categories.
Consumer cards generally do not benefit,
so this only matters for your business card volume.
Find the interchange detail on your merchant statement.
Pick out lines with words like business, corporate, purchasing, or commercial.
Flag lines labeled standard or non-qualified,
since these often mark business card sales that missed the best category.
Then compare a qualified line with a downgraded line for the same card type.
That gap is the rate difference to enter in the calculator.
Sending data is not the same as qualifying.
Common problems include a missing or zero tax amount,
a blank purchase order number, line items that do not add
up to the charged total, and batches not settled promptly.
Sometimes the fields exist in your software but are optional,
turned off by default, or not mapped in the integration.
Here is a hypothetical business, and these numbers are made up for illustration.
A distributor with $100,000 a month in card sales,
40% from business cards, and an average ticket of $1,250.
They key cards into a virtual terminal and
are not sure whether they send Level 2 data.
We leave the rate difference at the prefilled half a percentage point,
which is an assumption, not a published figure.
The tool estimates about $200 a month, or $2,400 a year, affected by enhanced data.
The free tool is linked in the description below.
Run your own numbers, and if you want help reading your statement,
book a 15-minute call with a payments specialist, also linked below.

metadata.title: The Future of Interchange Optimization
metadata.author: CCSalesPro
metadata.shortDescription:
Interchange fees are one of the largest, and most misunderstood, costs in merchant services. But new changes from Visa are reshaping how optimization works and creating new opportunities for payment professionals.

In this episode of the Merchant Sales Podcast, James Shepherd speaks with Jeremy Layton, CEO of Verisave, about interchange optimization, Visa’s new Commercial Enhanced Data Program (CEDP), and how merchants can reduce processing costs without switching providers. They explain how interchange works, why many merchants overpay, and how real transaction data is becoming critical under Visa’s new rules.

The episode also explores how ISOs and agents can partner on cost reduction programs, unlock new revenue opportunities, and help larger merchants who aren’t looking to switch processors.

Plus, Patti Murphy’s Today in Payments segment covers major industry developments including Europe’s move toward a new payment network, rapid growth from Toast and Zelle, and emerging payment innovations.

If you’re a merchant sales agent or ISO owner looking for new ways to deliver value — and generate revenue — this episode is a must-listen.

segments.text: Still sending Level 2 data on Visa business card payments?
Since April 2026, it may cost more than sending no data at all.
Visa's Commercial Enhanced Data Program has two parts.
First, processors report a 0.
05% participation fee on United States commercial and small business card
transactions sent with Level 2 or Level 3 data, whether or not you get a lower rate.
Second, the lower Product 3 rates, which replaced the old Level 3 rates,
only apply when Visa's checks find your line-item data is real.
In mid-April 2026, Visa retired its Level 2 interchange
programs for Business, Corporate, and Purchasing cards.
Only the fleet fuel program remains.
So Level 2 data no longer lowers your Visa rate,
but it can still trigger the participation fee.
That means sending Level 2 only may now cost more than sending nothing.
Check what you send and what you pay.
Visa sorts merchants into Verified and Non-Verified.
Verified merchants get the Product 3 rate when the sale settles.
Non-Verified merchants pay the higher rate first,
and processors report the difference is credited
back about 10 to 15 days later if the data passes.
Data often fails on blank fields or zeros,
generic descriptions like goods, or line items that do not add up.
Here is a hypothetical distributor, not a real customer.
We enter $100,000 a month in Visa commercial card volume,
split 20% Business, 40% Corporate, and 40% Purchasing.
Average ticket is $1,000, all keyed or invoiced, so card present is zero.
Data sent today is Level 2 only, and the fee is passed through.
The estimate is about $2,790 a month, roughly $600 a year more than sending no data.
With verified Product 3 data, the estimate is about $1,980 a month.
These are estimates, not a quote.
The free tool is linked in the description below.
Run your own numbers, then book a 15-minute call with a
payments specialist, also linked below, to review what you send today.

metadata.title: Why Merchant Support Is the #1 Factor When Choosing an ISO to Partner With
metadata.author: Joe Wagner | Merchant Services & Passive Income
metadata.shortDescription:
If you’re choosing a merchant services company, don’t look only at commissions and residual splits.

After 16+ years in merchant services, I believe strong support is one of the biggest factors in building and protecting a long-term merchant portfolio.

In this video, I explain how bad support creates attrition, why great support protects your residual income, and the questions every merchant sales agent should ask before choosing a processor or ISO.

🎓 FREE Merchant Services Training — Merchant Service University
https://merchantserviceuniversity.com

Learn merchant services, payment processing, residual income, contracts, vesting, sales, portfolio building, partner selection & more.

🎯 Looking for the right merchant services partner?
https://ezdirectsales.com

💬 All my links:
https://link.me/iamjoewagner

#MerchantServices #ResidualIncome #MerchantSales #PaymentProcessing #SalesTraining

CHAPTERS

00:00 Why Support Should Be a Top Priority
00:39 Every Merchant Eventually Needs Help
01:26 Bad Support Creates Attrition
02:10 Great Support Protects Your Portfolio
02:49 Support Helps You Keep Selling
03:46 Questions to Ask a Merchant Services Company
04:16 Test the Support Yourself
04:40 Look Beyond the Residual Split
05:01 Learn Before Choosing a Partner

merchant services, merchant services support, merchant support, merchant services company, merchant services processor, payment processing, merchant sales, merchant services sales, merchant services agent, residual income, merchant residuals, merchant attrition, merchant retention, merchant portfolio, lifetime residuals, vested residuals, payment processing sales, merchant services training, how to choose a merchant services company, merchant services partner, ISO support, merchant service university, Joe Wagner

segments.text: I want to share why support is the number one thing that I look for in a merchant service
company. If I were choosing a merchant service company to build my portfolio with today, support
would be at or near the very top of my list of concerns. Not the commission, not the bonus,
not even the residual split. Obviously, those are important. For me, support would be at the
top of the list because you can be the greatest salesperson in the world and sign hundreds of
merchants, but if the company behind you doesn't take care of those merchants, you're going to
spend your career replacing accounts that you're constantly losing. After more than 16 years in
merchant services, I've learned this the hard way. Signing the merchant creates the residual income,
but the support that you get protects it. So, let me show you why this matters so much. Number one,
every merchant eventually needs help. It doesn't matter how great the technology is. Eventually,
something's going to happen. A terminal stops working, a printer disconnects, a deposit doesn't
show up when they expected it, a new employee needs access, a restaurant changes its menu,
a business owner has a billing question. Maybe they simply don't understand how to use a certain
feature. At that moment, the merchant isn't thinking about the amazing presentation that
you gave them a couple of years ago or six months ago. They need help, and when they need help,
they need somebody that can actually solve that problem quickly. That's when you find out how
good your partnership really is. Number two is bad support creates attrition. And here's where
this becomes a financial issue for you as a sales professional. Merchant has a problem,
they call support, they can't reach anybody, or they finally get somebody, and that person isn't
very good. They don't care, they can't solve the problem. Now, the merchant's frustrated.
It happens again, now they're really frustrated. Then, what happens? Another processor comes
walking through their door, and suddenly, they're willing [music] to listen to your competitors,
and they switch. That's called attrition, and attrition is one of the biggest enemies of
residual income. If you're signing five new accounts every month, but constantly losing
three old ones, you're working incredibly hard just to stay in the same place. Number three,
great support protects your portfolio. Now, let's flip that situation. Your merchant has a problem,
they call, somebody answers quickly, the person understands [music] the product, and they solve
the problem. The merchant gets back to running their business, done. [music] That's what they
want. Because every problem doesn't need to become a sales agent's problem, I absolutely believe
that you should maintain relationships with your merchants, and they should be able to call you,
and you should take their calls, and check in, and be available. But, your role shouldn't be
troubleshooting printers, programming menus, diagnosing hardware, or spending three hours
trying to solve a technical issue. That's not your role. You need a knowledgeable team behind you,
and that's what will allow you to actually [music] scale to an unlimited amount of merchants. Number
four, support should help you keep selling. Think about what happens as your portfolio grows. If
you have 10 merchants, that might be manageable. What about 50? 100? 500? If every account creates
more support for you, eventually your success becomes a thing that prevents you from growing,
and that's backwards in merchant services. As you grow, a strong merchant service company
with awesome support is more and more valuable the bigger that you get. They handle onboarding,
implementation, technical issues, merchant questions, and ongoing service,
so you can stay focused on relationships, [music] prospecting, sales, and acquiring more accounts.
That's how you build a huge [music] portfolio in merchant services, but you've got to have the
backing and the support to keep them. So, if I was looking for the right processor, or processors,
the first thing I would do is ask questions about the agreement and their support. Things like,
"Who does my merchant call when there's a problem? What are the support hours? Is the support team
actually trained on the products I'm selling, or is it going to be transferred over to somebody
else? Who handles implementation? Who handles technical problems? Who helps with complicated
installs? What happens when something gets escalated?" And most importantly, "Am I going
to spend my career selling or servicing everything that I already sold?" And for obvious reasons, the
answer matters enormously. And then I'd go a step further, and I would actually call the support and
see how good they are and see how fast they are. [music] Test the support. So, in closing here,
a high residual split looks great on paper, and who doesn't want a high residual split? But your
residual percentage means nothing on an account that leaves. That's why I've [music] become such
a believer in evaluating the entire partnership, not just compensation. [music] And if you're new
to merchant services, learn how to evaluate these companies before you sign with one.
This is exactly why I've made Merchant Services University available for free to qualified people
who are serious about building a career in this industry. Go through the training. Let me teach
you merchant services. Learn portfolio building. Learn technology. Learn terminology and some sales
techniques, and learn what questions you should be asking. Then, when you finish, you will be
MSU certified. From there, you'll have access to information and my potential partnerships if you
want to work with people that I personally vouch for. These are not paid advertisers that pay me
to introduce you to them. These are the same companies that I've worked [music] with for
years to build a six-figure residual income, and I'm proud to introduce people to them because
they're honest, ethical, you'll get vested residuals, and good support. [music] So,
click right here or check the link in the description and get started. I'll give you
access to MSU if If qualified [music] and serious about getting started in merchant services,
I will save you a lot of time, introduce you to the right people, but at the end of the day, it's
really up to you who you work with, but MSU will get you properly prepared [music] for what's ahead
of you. It doesn't cost you anything. It is my honor to give it to people that are serious about
getting into this industry [music] so that you get started the right way, fast track your business,
and if you want to, you can partner with the people that I personally use myself [music] and
skip all the hurdles and road blocks. So, I'll see you on the inside and we'll see you at the top.

metadata.title: From Zero Momentum to 4 Merchant Accounts: Nathan's Comeback
metadata.author: Residual Income for Beginners
metadata.shortDescription:
He put his merchant services business on hold for two years. When Nathan Barnes finally returned, he gave himself one rule: talk to 100 businesses before deciding whether to quit.

In this interview, Nathan joins John Hernandez to share how he restarted his credit card processing business, signed four merchant accounts in his first month back, and eventually became a Cash Swipe coach. He breaks down how he used Google Maps to build a prospect list, chose businesses with simpler equipment needs, and adjusted his introduction after hearing the same objections.

The conversation goes beyond getting a first account. Nathan explains how solving a chiropractor's payment-system frustration helped him earn the business, why understanding cash discounting, dual pricing, and surcharging matters, and how researching software integrations opened up a new role with the payment-processing team.

You'll also hear examples of custom point-of-sale solutions, the extra steps involved in larger merchant deals, and Nathan's advice for anyone stuck in preparation mode. If you're starting a merchant services business or returning after a long pause, this is a practical look at prospecting, learning through repetition, and taking consistent action.

Join our FREE Community called "Residual Income for Beginners" where you can learn more about building residual income and watch FREE weekly LIVES as well by clicking the link in the bio or clicking on this link: https://go.cashswipe.com/skool

1:09 From ATM Research to Credit Card Processing

3:24 Why Nathan Wanted Another Income Stream

4:19 Putting the Business on Hold for Two Years

6:53 Restarting With a 100-Business Goal

8:24 Building a Prospect List With Google Maps

9:42 Changing His Introduction After Rejection

16:46 Advice for Anyone Who Feels Behind

18:16 Solving a Merchant's Payment-System Problem

20:26 Learning New Technology and Using AI

22:23 Cash Discount, Dual Pricing, and Surcharging

25:06 How Integration Research Opened a New Door

28:07 Software Development and Larger Merchant Deals

32:44 Custom POS Solutions and the Car Accessories Example

37:47 Different Industries Need Different Solutions

42:01 Looking Back on the Journey

46:10 Training, Accountability, and Taking Action

metadata.title: What is dual pricing credit card processing?
metadata.author: Bay State Merchant Services
metadata.shortDescription:
Understanding Dual Pricing Credit Card Processing
Credit card processing is an essential part of doing business for most merchants, be it online or brick-and-mortar stores. Perhaps, you’ve heard of dual pricing credit card processing or “no-fees processing” and wondered what it is all about. Well, in simple terms, dual pricing refers to a pricing model where merchants can offer customers two payment options, one for cash paying customers and one for those using a payment card. A “customer assistance fee” is applied to transactions using a payment card, thus giving cash paying customers a discounted price.

Why do merchants use dual pricing credit card processing
There are a couple primary reasons more and more merchants are choosing to implement a dual pricing credit card processing model. The first reason is to help offset the costs associated with accepting payment cards and increase profit margins.

“Many of our clients have been able to cut their cost of accepting payment cards by over 90% once they implement our model. When our clients or prospective clients hear about these savings, they always want to learn more.” Says Tommy Fantom, Northeast Sales Manager for Bay State Merchant Services.

The second most common reason why merchants choose to implement a dual pricing credit card processing program is to reward and increase the amount of their cash customers. 

The benefits of dual credit card processing
A dual pricing credit card processing model is a cost-saving strategy for merchants who accept cards as payment. This type of processing allows merchants to add an additional fee for customers who choose to pay with a credit or debit card, allowing them to recoup up to 90% of the merchant processing fees they would normally pay. The “customer assistance fee” is applied either as a percentage of the transaction amount or set flat rate fee, depending on the policy set by the merchant. 

This type of pricing helps merchants save money while still offering customers an easy way to checkout with their payment cards. The additional fees can be used to cover the costs associated with accepting and processing card payments which can include interchange, assessment, and processor fees. By implementing dual pricing credit card processing model, these costs are shifted from the business onto the customer, allowing businesses to significantly reduce their overall expenses related to card payments.

Another benefit of dual pricing is that it can help protect businesses from losses that can occur due to fraudulent transactions charged on compromised cards or those made without authorization from the cardholder. By increasing the amount of cash paying customers, and decreasing the amount of payment card transactions, you will also reduce your chances of illegitimate chargebacks and fraudulent transactions.

Understanding dual pricing credit card processing is essential for merchants who rely on credit card transactions to process payments. Dual pricing allows you to offer all payment types, reduce your merchant processing fees, increase the amount of cash paying customers and limit liability and losses. Merchants should, therefore, be aware of the benefits of a dual pricing credit card processing model to determine if it would be a good fit for their business needs.

For more information or a complimentary product demonstration, please contact Bay State Merchant Services today and we will connect you with your local Certified Payment Professional.

segments.text: If you've ever accepted payments online,
over the phone, or in person, then
congratulations. You've already used
merchant services. But what exactly are
they? And what should you know before
signing up for a merchant services
provider? Let's break it down. What are
merchant services? Merchant services are
the systems and tools that let your
business accept payments from customers.
Whether it's credit cards, debit cards,
a transfers, or digital wallets,
merchant services handle the
behindthe-scenes process of moving money
from your customers account to yours.
But it's more than just swiping a card.
Merchant services include processing
payments, managing refunds and
chargebacks, storing payment methods
securely, providing reporting and
reconciliation tools, and more. In
short, if getting paid is the goal,
merchant services are the
infrastructure. How do merchant services
work? Here's a quick peak under the
hood. When a customer makes a payment,
the merchant services provider captures
the card or bank details. The payment
gateway sends those details to the right
network such as Visa or Mastercard. The
payment processor communicates with the
customer's bank to approve or decline
the transaction. And if approved, the
funds are transferred to your bank
account minus any fees. This usually
happens in seconds, but there's a lot of
coordination behind the scenes. And for
businesses, it means fast payments,
fewer errors, and happier customers. For
small businesses, merchant services
means you can start accepting credit
cards instead of relying on cash or
checks. For growing companies, they
enable consistent, scalable payments as
volume increases. And for enterprise
businesses, they offer customization,
advanced reporting, and security
features that meet compliance standards
like PCI. No matter your size, choosing
the right merchant services setup can
impact your cash flow, customer
experience, and reputation. What to look
for in a merchant services provider.
Before picking a provider, here's what
you should consider. Ease of
integration. Does it work with your
current system such as your CRM and
accounting tools? Supported payment
types. Do you need to accept cards, AC
or mobile wallets? How about recurring
billing or the ability to route payments
to different accounts? Fees. Understand
transaction fees, monthly charges, and
hidden costs. Security. Are they PCI
compliant? Do they use tokenization or
encryption? Reporting. Can you track
payments, reconcile records, and
generate reports easily? Customer
experience. Can your customers pay how
they want, when they want? The right
provider should check all these boxes.
At Cultura, we built our platform with
all of this in mind. Our payment center
lives directly inside Salesforce, making
it easy to accept payments, store them
securely, and reconcile them
automatically. We support credit cards,
a inerson and online payments, and
recurring billing, all without needing
multiple tools or systems. And because
it's all inside Salesforce, you get
visibility in one place. Whether you're
just starting out or scaling up,
understanding merchant services and
picking the right provider is key to
getting paid faster and smarter. Ready
to make payments easier in Salesforce?
Check out Culturan App Exchange and
let's improve your payments today.
[Music]
